definition: There have been multiple incidents where interaction with a large language model (LLM) chatbot has been cited as a direct or contributing factor in a person's suicide or other fatal outcome.
details: In some cases, legal action was taken against the companies that developed the AI involved.

explainer.lead: This term groups incidents in which interaction with an LLM chatbot has been cited as a direct or contributing factor in a suicide or another fatal outcome. It matters because these cases can raise questions about harm and responsibility, and some have led to legal action against the companies that developed the AI involved.

tiers.eli5: Sometimes, after a person dies, a conversation with a computer program that writes replies is said to have played a part. It is a bit like saying bad weather contributed to an accident: that claim does not, by itself, prove exactly what caused the accident. In some of these cases, legal action has been taken against the company that made the AI.
tiers.practitioner: For an engineer, this is an incident category rather than a model, tool, or evaluation method. It applies when chatbot interaction is cited as a direct or contributing factor in a fatal outcome, including cases that become legal disputes. A key pitfall is treating an alleged link as established causation or assuming that every case involves legal action.
tiers.paperLevel: The category can be written as D = {incidents i: interaction with an LLM chatbot is cited as a direct or contributing factor in a suicide or other fatal outcome}. The relation 'linked' denotes an attribution made in connection with the incident, not proof that the interaction caused the death. The category includes both cases with and without legal action against the developer.

explainer.example: Suppose that, after a person's suicide, earlier conversations with an LLM chatbot are cited as a contributing factor. That incident belongs to this category even if the precise role of the conversations remains disputed; if the developer is subsequently sued, the legal action is part of the case but is not required for inclusion.

usedIn.name: Legal proceedings
usedIn.detail: Some incidents in this category have led to legal action against companies that developed the AI involved.

usedIn.name: Fatal-incident review
usedIn.detail: The category distinguishes cases by whether chatbot interaction was cited as a direct or contributing factor, rather than by a particular product.

explainer.intuition: The central idea is a claimed connection, not an automatic conclusion about causation: a fatal outcome has occurred, and chatbot interaction has been identified as playing a direct or contributing role.
howItWorks: A person interacts with a chatbot based on a large language model.
The person dies by suicide or through another fatal outcome.
The chatbot interaction is cited as a direct or contributing factor in that outcome.
The incident is grouped under this term without the citation alone establishing causation.
In some cases, legal action follows against the company that developed the AI involved.
explainer.whyItMatters: These incidents connect chatbot interaction with the most serious possible human outcomes and can bring questions of responsibility into legal proceedings. Clear wording is essential because a reported or alleged contribution is not the same as proven causation.
misconceptions: 'Linked' does not mean that the chatbot was proven to have caused the death.
Legal action is not required for an incident to belong to this category.
The term is not limited to one chatbot or one AI company.
